steps.text: This video is for the person who looks after the Report Builder: who may build and see reports, how to move reports to another site, what the limits mean on large data, and what to do when something does not work.

Open Access Control, Roles, and edit a role. Search its permissions for custom reports. Build reports and manage own custom reports and views lets a person design reports and views, and change and delete their own.

View all custom reports lets a person run every report, whoever owns it. Manage all custom reports and views lets them change and delete every report and view, and it includes the two permissions above.
Share custom reports publicly and through share links is the one that lets a person share a report with the Anonymous role, and create share links.
Search for report groups. Manage report groups lets a person create, change and delete the groups reports are listed under. Manage all custom reports and views includes it.

chapters.title: See it work
chapters.subtitle: A role with no permission, then with one

steps.text: This is the Reports menu of a person whose role has none of these permissions. It lists the reports they may run, but there is no Report Builder.
In the role, tick Build reports and manage own custom reports and views, and save.
Now the same person has Report Builder under Reports, and builds reports of their own. They see their own reports, and the ones shared with them, and no one else's.

chapters.title: Bring reports to another site
chapters.subtitle: Import with the Report Designs step

steps.text: To bring reports onto a site, import them. Under Tools, Deployments, JSON Import takes a recipe with the Report Designs step, and Package Import takes the same in a package file.

Click Import. The import matches each report by its identifier: a report that exists is replaced, and one that does not is created, so the same file can be imported again. Share links are never imported.
The reports and their groups are now in the Report Builder. Each one keeps its owner when a user with the same user name exists on the site, and belongs to the person who ran the import otherwise.

chapters.title: Large data and limits
chapters.subtitle: What to tell the people who build reports

steps.text: The builder reads each data set in batches and never holds a whole data set in memory. Big joins and totals use temporary files on the server, so they are slower, not wrong.

A report that reads more rows than the limit says so with a warning, and the numbers cover only the rows it read. Add a shorter period or another filter, or ask for the limits to be raised in the site's configuration.
A new report starts with the last 30 days of its main date. For big data, keep a date filter on every report, and use a scheduled view for data that is heavy to prepare.
No Report Builder under Reports: the feature may be off, or the person lacks the build permission. People who only run shared reports see Shared Reports instead.
Fewer records than expected: the date filter of a new report is the last 30 days. Pick a longer period, or All time.
Totals too high after a join: a join repeats a row for each match. Count distinct values, or sum from the data set that has one row per record.
A shared report shows data its viewer cannot open: that is expected, since it reads data with its owner's access. Share only what viewers should see.
Give the five permissions with care, move reports with a deployment plan, and keep a date filter on large data. Thanks for watching.
